questions.explanation:
## Why This Is Asked
Tests ability to design a small, extensible plugin system using runtime registries and the separation of concerns between formatting and sinking.

## Key Concepts
- Registry pattern for dynamic extensibility
- Strategy/Factory for pluggable formatters
- Async I/O and backpressure in sinks
- Graceful shutdown and error containment

## Code Example
```typescript
interface Formatter { format(msg: string, level: string): string; }
interface Sink { write(data: string): Promise<void>; }
class Registry {
  private formats = new Map<string, Formatter>();
  private sinks = new Map<string, Sink>();
  registerFormat(name: string, f: Formatter): void
  getFormat(name: string): Formatter
  registerSink(name: string, s: Sink): void
  getSink(name: string): Sink
}
```

## Follow-up Questions
- How would you test runtime registration of new formats?
- How would you prevent a slow sink from blocking others?

questions.explanation:
## Why This Is Asked
Beginner-friendly exploration of extensibility and non-blocking I/O: add new sinks without changing core, and isolate failures per sink.

## Key Concepts
- Strategy/Plug-in pattern for runtime extension
- Registry mapping names to Sink implementations
- Non-blocking writes via per-sink queuing and worker pool
- Fault isolation and graceful degradation

## Code Example
```typescript
interface Sink { write(msg: string): Promise<void> }
class Registry { addSink(name: string, s: Sink): void; getSinks(): Sink[] }
class Logger { constructor(private reg: Registry) ; log(msg: string): void { for (const s of reg.getSinks()) s.write(msg); } }
```

## Follow-up Questions
- How would you test sink isolation and backpressure?
- How would you implement graceful shutdown for all sinks?

## Why This Is Asked
Introduce a new angle: runtime-extensible evaluation logic for feature flags to reflect real-world needs in large orgs.

## Key Concepts
- Strategy pattern for evaluators
- Registry for dynamic extension
- Composite rule composition (anyOf/allOf)
- EvalContext design and caching for performance

## Code Example
```typescript
interface Evaluator { evaluate(ctx: EvalContext): boolean }
type EvalContext = { user: any; time: Date; attrs: any }
class EvaluatorRegistry {
  register(name: string, factory: (cfg: any)=>Evaluator): void
  resolve(name: string, cfg: any): Evaluator
}
```

## Follow-up Questions
- How to model evaluation order and short-circuit semantics?
- How to handle cross-feature conflicts and auditing of evaluator registrations?

## Why This Is Asked
Tests runtime extensibility, registry design, non-blocking fan-out, and routing policy decisions. Also evaluates trade-offs between Strategy and Chain in a pluggable auditing pipeline.

## Key Concepts
- Runtime plugin registry and factories
- Non-blocking, bounded concurrency routing
- Per-event routing rules and backpressure handling
- Strategy vs Chain trade-offs in routing

## Code Example
```typescript
interface Event { source: string; severity: 'info'|'warning'|'error'; category: string; payload: any }
interface Auditor { log(event: Event): Promise<void> }
type AuditorFactory = () => Auditor
class AuditorRegistry { register(name: string, f: AuditorFactory); create(name: string): Auditor }
class Router { constructor(private reg: AuditorRegistry, private rules: Array<(e:Event)=>boolean>); route(e:Event): Promise<void> }
```

## Follow-up Questions
- How would you test the registry and routing guarantees?
- What metrics would you collect for backpressure and throughput?

questions.explanation:
## Why This Is Asked
Tests understanding of open/closed principles, plugin registries, and runtime configurability for cross-cutting concerns like logging.

## Key Concepts
- Strategy pattern
- Registry / plugin architecture
- Thread-safety and dynamic configuration
- Separation of concerns in logging

## Code Example
```javascript
interface LogEvent { level: string; message: string; ts: number; }
interface LogFormatter { format(event: LogEvent): string; }
class JSONFormatter implements LogFormatter { format(e: LogEvent) { return JSON.stringify(e); } }
class KVFormatter implements LogFormatter { format(e: LogEvent) { return `ts=${e.ts} level=${e.level} msg='${e.message}'`; } }
class Registry<T> { private map = new Map<string, T>(); register(name: string, v: T){ this.map.set(name, v); } get(name: string): T | undefined { return this.map.get(name); } }
```

## Follow-up Questions
- How would you handle thread-safety in a multi-threaded environment?
- How to test registering and switching formatters in isolation?
